reason: E1 shows in-flight oxidation occurs and can increase α-Al2O3 content in a similar HEA, but does not demonstrate control over preferential oxidation or link it to improved scale adhesion/spallation resistance above 900 °C. premises: In-flight oxidation during HVOF spraying can be controlled to promote preferential oxidation of Al in FeNiCoCrMoAl-based HEAs.
Preferential oxidation of Al leads to formation of α-Al2O3.
Al2O3 scales grow slowly, are stable, and resist cracking/spallation above 900 °C.
Si or Mn in place of Al leads to less adherent, unstable oxide scales under the same conditions.
Controlled in-flight oxidation is necessary to achieve the beneficial Al2O3 scale; without it, oxide layers are less adherent.
